status: Discovery map, not a completed causal account

themes.title: What families give up to pay the bills
themes.meaning: Compare money spent with care or protection left out.

themes.title: Who gives up time
themes.meaning: Compare unpaid help with time spent using a product; the reasons and benefits differ.

themes.title: Who can get an answer or change a decision
themes.meaning: Look for actual choices and responses before claiming that trust or power changed.

nodes.title: The price on the screen is only part of the cost
nodes.summary: Fees, rewards and payment timing can leave households with different costs for the same purchase.
nodes.question: Who pays beyond the purchase price?
nodes.limit: The current payment finding relies on an HBS summary; the underlying paper still needs review.

nodes.title: Keeping a home also means paying to protect it
nodes.summary: Insurance bills and gaps in coverage belong in the housing affordability story.
nodes.question: Who can afford protection?
nodes.limit: The packet does not establish that insurance changes caused families to move.

nodes.title: People can pay the bills by giving up care
nodes.summary: Skipped treatment can keep spending down while leaving a need unmet.
nodes.question: What did the household give up?
nodes.limit: Reported skipped care does not establish later health or job outcomes.

nodes.title: A family can pay for care with time
nodes.summary: Unpaid help uses hours that could otherwise go to work, rest or other family needs.
nodes.question: Whose time covers the need?
nodes.limit: Care hours are not automatically lost work hours; employment effects need separate evidence.

nodes.title: Personal finances and national mood can move apart
nodes.summary: People judge the economy through both their circumstances and their expectations about the country.
nodes.question: What explains the gap between experience and belief?
nodes.limit: The surveys do not show that bills caused a vote; party identity can shape economic views.

nodes.title: Business counts do not tell us who belongs to a place
nodes.summary: Applications, lasting jobs and locally rooted owners describe different parts of a town's economy.
nodes.question: What stays in the community?
nodes.limit: Birth-state location is not hometown attachment; civic effects remain questions.

nodes.title: A quicker reply may still leave a problem open
nodes.summary: Response speed, a friendly tone and successful resolution need separate measures.
nodes.question: Can someone actually fix the problem?
nodes.limit: The service experiment is one setting; its results do not establish a general loss of appeal rights.

nodes.title: A useful app can still make leaving difficult
nodes.summary: The reason a person stays matters when longer conversations benefit the company.
nodes.question: Does staying reflect help or pressure?
nodes.limit: Companion-app studies do not represent all chatbot users or establish lasting harm.

edges.relation: Cost can lead people to use less protection or care
edges.limit: Parallel household choices; neither packet proves the same people face both.

edges.relation: An unmet care need may require more family time
edges.limit: Check whether skipped treatment actually increases unpaid care; this has not been shown here.

edges.relation: Less paid work could leave less money for bills
edges.limit: Check earnings around the start of care and borrowing afterward.

edges.relation: Company goals and customer goals may differ when a conversation continues
edges.limit: Longer contact may mean useful help, an unresolved problem or pressure to stay.

edges.relation: A rise in housing costs could affect who can own a local business
edges.limit: Needs linked evidence on owners, housing costs and business moves.

edges.relation: Financial pressure might change whom people blame
edges.limit: Compare changes within the same people and account for party identity.

edges.relation: Difficulty paying for care may become a public concern
edges.limit: Concern and skipped care are separate observations, not a proven causal chain.

edges.relation: Repeated unresolved problems might weaken trust
edges.limit: No direct evidence of that chain in the current packet.
